jsnell · Nov 28, 2026

This is just a deeply confused take from Sweeney.

The capabilities of the model after training are what they are. There is no silent degradation on top of that. Sweeney should know this, since he is replying to a post that explained exactly this.

If you're saying that releasing a model that's not the absolute best it can be at everything is sabotage, you run into problems pretty quickly. For example, every model could be better if you just trained it for a day longer. And, by induction, by training it forever and not releasing it at all.

Or within a fixed budget, models could be better at speaking French if you increased the proportion of French langauge training data, but then that would come at the expense of say German. Not doing that isn't trying to sabotage France.

There's an endless number of specialized domains that you could be training the model to be better at by e.g. having RL environments for them, but that would clearly be bad ideas. We don't want to train models to be the ultimate biological weapons developers, black-hat hackers, or phishing scammers. Not doing that training, isn't "sabotage".

0xbadcafebee · Nov 28, 2026

The model's capability degrades silently literally all the time. Quantization/cache quantization, cache eviction, preemption, memory pressure/fragmentation, batching, fuzzy or quantized MTP, sparse attention, token eviction, activation clipping, MoE precision loss, floating-point variance, hell even the literal temperature. All of these degrade the model's capability, and they happen all the time, without you knowing. You need to be very specific about what you count as degradation.

What people are calling "sabotage" here is incorrect. Sabotage is the deliberate destruction or damage of a thing, not giving you less of a thing. The model still works fine, it's just working at 90% power instead of 100%.

If the manufacturer of Doritos put 90% of the normal amount of chips in every bag, they are not sabotaging you or the chips, they're just giving you less. Sabotage would be putting a little hole in the bag so the chips go stale and you can't use them anymore. Another example: Lots of cars have the capability for more horsepower in their engines, and the manufacturer rolls some of the horsepower back. They aren't sabotaging the car.
